title: Build with Zeron and AI
description: Find the right components, read their contracts, and let your coding agent integrate them into your project.
development: Component search, documentation and Skills downloads are available. Verified component installation commands are not available on this deployment yet.
release: This deployment uses a published catalog. Your agent will check the installation combination for your project before returning a command.
connectBody: Add a remote MCP server in a coding tool that supports Streamable HTTP. Copy the address below from the deployment you are using. The server reads public Zeron documentation; it does not edit your project or keep a conversation history.
clientStatus: Check whether this browser can discover all five Zeron tools. This does not verify your coding client or enable component installation.
skillsBody: Zeron Page Builder guides page integration. Swap to Zeron UI manages migration scope, source ownership, and completion evidence. Read the installation guide to install both, verify their hashes, and preserve your local edits.
docsBody: You can use Zeron without MCP. Start with the short index, select a catalog item, and read its Markdown. Keep the catalog version when following fixed release links.
promptsBody: These prompts describe integration tasks. Ask your agent to inspect your project first and report what it actually verified.

prompts.list: Build a resource list with Zeron in this project. Inspect the framework, React/Tailwind versions and existing shell first. Search components, retain catalogVersion, and read candidate guides. Preserve navigation and scroll ownership. Connect my data through typed adapters, covering loading, empty, error, permission and pagination states. Request a verified dry-run command before installation. Report adopted components and actual checks.
prompts.detail: Build a Zeron resource detail view in this project. Inspect the installed APIs and choose a matching detail layout. Preserve the list query when returning, use the public summary, action and content slots, and connect real read/update callbacks. Cover loading, missing resource, error, read-only access and narrow screens. Verify the selected catalog and installation combination before installing, and report remaining integration gaps.
prompts.settings: Build a settings page with Zeron in this project. Reuse the existing shell and installed public form APIs. Connect typed load/save callbacks and server validation. Preserve unsaved edits, disable unauthorized changes, and cover loading, save failure, retry and success. Verify the framework and installation combination before installing. Run available type, build and interaction checks and report the results.

troubleshooting.connection: Check the full /api/mcp address, Streamable HTTP support, and the deployment's access protection. A browser GET returning 405 is expected; it does not prove tool calls have failed.
troubleshooting.version: Read the immutable catalog URL saved from the earlier response, or search again using this deployment's current catalog. An older deployment may not contain a newer tool snapshot.
troubleshooting.install: Some entries are demos or references. Others may require Next.js or an installation combination that has not been verified. Inspect the tool's reason and confirm your local framework; do not force an overwrite.
troubleshooting.language: Use the root /api/mcp endpoint, without an /en or /zh-cn prefix. Recheck your client's protocol support and deployment access settings.
troubleshooting.sourceTitle: The guide differs from installed code
troubleshooting.source: Check the installed component's source and types, then select its matching Registry and catalog version. The installed public API is authoritative.

connectionPassed: Connected: all five Zeron tools were discovered. Continue with your client setup below.
connectionFailed: Connection check failed or timed out. Confirm the address and network access, then try again. You can still use the documentation links below.
codexSetup: Run this command with the Codex CLI, then open a new session and confirm that the Zeron tools are available. If a server named zeron already exists, inspect its configuration before replacing it.
cursorSetup: Merge this entry into the mcpServers object in your project’s .cursor/mcp.json, keeping any existing servers. Enable Zeron in Cursor’s MCP settings.
localNotice: This address points to this machine. Keep the local server running and use a client on this machine. A remote or cloud client needs a deployment it can reach.
installBoundary: Skills can be downloaded and installed independently. Component installation commands require a verified published CLI, Registry and target framework combination; a successful connection check does not remove this requirement.
